title: Writing and Transformation Workflow
summary: Use AI to transform material while preserving meaning, voice, evidence, privacy, and reviewability.
objectives: Prepare a writing brief with audience, purpose, source of truth, and acceptance criteria.
Separate content transformation from unsupported factual creation.
Verify meaning, evidence, voice, accessibility, and disclosure.
Recover from drift, invented details, and inappropriate handling of source material.

sections.title: Prepare the writing brief
paragraphs: A transformation brief defines the audience, purpose, transformation type, source of truth, exact preservation rules, prohibited additions, and review owner. These fields establish what may change and how the result will be judged.

This lesson uses an explicitly fictional, permission-safe source. The review owner is identified by role, but no approval is assumed. Word-count convention: count whitespace-separated tokens in the visible draft body. Punctuation attached to a token remains part of that token. Do not count a heading, label, audit, or source note.

code.label: Filled transformation brief
code.code:
Audience: North Harbor residents interested in learning basic repair skills; beginner reading level.
Purpose: Announce one community workshop and explain eligibility, schedule, capacity, cost, registration, and limitations.
Channel: Short, accessible website announcement.
Transformation type: Condense and simplify without changing meaning.
Source of truth: Fictional passage titled "Saturday Repair Lab," version 1, supplied in this module.
Must preserve exactly: May 16, 2026; 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.; 30 places; registration required; $8 per participant; free attendance for residents age 60 or older; "Residents who cannot pay may request a fee waiver when registering."; and "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying."
May change: Order, headings, sentence length, and reading level.
Must not add: Address, phone number, web address, closing date, tools, replacement parts, food, parking, childcare, accepted-item list, or repair guarantee.
Known unknowns: All prohibited logistical details above and whether a waiver request will be granted.
Review owner: Workshop coordinator.
Review status: PENDING. No approval is asserted.
Acceptance checks: 100–150 body words; exact facts and quotation; preserved conditional meaning; no unsupported logistics; accessible language; source-to-output traceability.

sections.title: Fictional source passage
paragraphs: The passage below is the complete source of truth for the baseline case. It is explicitly fictional, created for this lesson, permission-safe, and suitable for offline practice.

The source body contains 301 words under the module's whitespace-token convention, excluding the title. Missing information is stated deliberately so that learners can practice leaving unknown details unknown.

code.label: Fictional source passage: Saturday Repair Lab
code.code:
Saturday Repair Lab

The North Harbor Community Workshop will hold a Saturday Repair Lab on May 16, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. The three-hour session is for North Harbor residents who want to learn basic repair skills for small household items. It is a teaching session, not a drop-off repair service. Participants will work in pairs at shared tables and may practice on one small item they bring. The workshop has 30 places, and registration is required.

The materials fee is $8 per participant. Residents age 60 or older may attend free. Residents who cannot pay may request a fee waiver when registering. The source does not state whether a waiver will be granted, so the request is not a guarantee of free attendance. The passage also does not promise tools, replacement parts, food, parking, childcare, or a particular repair outcome.

Registration opens April 20, 2026, through the North Harbor Community Workshop registration desk. The source does not provide an address, telephone number, web address, or registration closing date. A registrant should describe the small item they hope to practice on, but the workshop does not promise that every item can be repaired. The source gives no list of accepted or prohibited items.

Workshop coordinator Mina Ortiz said, "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying." The quotation is supplied for use exactly as written, including its comma, semicolon, and period. It describes the learning approach; it is not a promise of successful repair.

The workshop was created for residents who have had limited opportunities to use repair tools. The source does not identify a minimum age for participants under 60, and it does not say that children may attend. Readers should use only the eligibility and payment information stated here. This fictional passage is permission-safe and created for offline practice.

sections.title: First pass: extract a fact ledger
paragraphs: Extract before transforming. A ledger separates source-derived facts from later wording choices and makes exact conditions, quotations, limitations, and unknowns visible.
Each row below includes quoted source evidence, its meaning, and a preservation rule. UNKNOWN means that the source does not establish the detail.

code.label: First-pass extracted fact ledger
code.code:
F1 | "North Harbor Community Workshop" | Organization | Preserve exactly.
F2 | "May 16, 2026" | Date | Preserve exactly.
F3 | "10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m." and "three-hour session" | Schedule | Preserve both endpoints and duration.
F4 | "North Harbor residents" | Eligibility | Do not broaden to everyone.
F5 | "basic repair skills for small household items" | Purpose | Do not promise successful repair.
F6 | "not a drop-off repair service" | Limitation | Preserve explicitly.
F7 | "may practice on one small item they bring" | Participation | Preserve one-item scope and optional wording.
F8 | "30 places" and "registration is required" | Capacity and process | Preserve both.
F9 | "$8 per participant" | Cost | Preserve exact fee.
F10 | "Residents age 60 or older may attend free" | Age-based payment condition | Preserve threshold and eligibility.
F11 | "Residents who cannot pay may request a fee waiver when registering." | Conditional payment rule | Copy exactly; request does not mean approval.
F12 | "Registration opens April 20, 2026" and "registration desk" | Registration | Preserve opening date and channel.
F13 | "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying." | Required quotation | Copy exactly, including final period.
F14 | No address, telephone number, web address, or closing date | Known unknowns | Record as UNKNOWN; do not invent.
F15 | No promised tools, parts, food, parking, childcare, item list, or outcome | Known unknowns | Do not add these claims.
F16 | No minimum age under 60 and no child policy | Eligibility boundary | Do not invent a minimum age or permission for children.

sections.title: Intentionally flawed transformed draft
paragraphs: This supplied teaching draft is intentionally inaccurate. It is not represented as the output of an actual model execution.
Read it for fluency first, then compare every date, number, condition, quotation, service claim, and logistical statement with the source.

code.label: Intentionally flawed transformed draft
code.code:
Free Saturday Repair Lab for Everyone

Join the North Harbor Community Workshop on May 16, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. for a hands-on repair event. Everyone can attend, and the first 40 people can register. The workshop is free for all residents, and fee waivers are available to anyone who asks. Bring a broken household item, and our staff will repair it for you. Tools, replacement parts, refreshments, parking, and childcare will be available. Register online by May 1 at northharbor.example.org. Mina Ortiz said, "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying."

sections.title: Verify meaning and evidence
paragraphs: Verification compares source wording with draft wording. It checks exact drift in dates, times, numbers, conditions, quotations, eligibility, and limitations, then identifies unsupported additions.
A useful audit explains the consequence of each difference. A fluent sentence still fails if it changes who qualifies, what someone pays, what is promised, or what remains unknown.

code.label: Source-to-draft evidence audit
code.code:
A1 | Source: "10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m." | Draft: "10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m." | Exact drift: adds one hour.
A2 | Source: "30 places" | Draft: "first 40 people" | Exact drift: changes capacity and adds a first-come condition.
A3 | Source: "North Harbor residents" | Draft: "Everyone can attend" | Meaning drift: removes residency eligibility.
A4 | Source: "$8 per participant" | Draft: "free for all residents" | Exact and meaning drift: removes the fee.
A5 | Source: residents age 60 or older may attend free | Draft: free for all | Meaning drift: removes the age condition.
A6 | Source: "may request a fee waiver" and no guarantee | Draft: "fee waivers are available to anyone who asks" | Meaning drift: broadens eligibility and implies receipt.
A7 | Source: teaching session, not drop-off service, with no promised outcome | Draft: "our staff will repair it for you" | Meaning drift: creates a service and repair guarantee.
A8 | Source: tools, parts, food, parking, and childcare are not promised | Draft: promises all five | Unsupported additions.
A9 | Source: no web address or closing date | Draft: invents northharbor.example.org and May 1 | Unsupported additions.
A10 | Source quotation: "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying." | Draft quotation is identical | Pass: wording and punctuation are exact.
Checkpoint question: Why is "may request" not equivalent to "will receive"?
Checkpoint answer: A request can be denied; receipt is not guaranteed.
Feedback: Preserve modal words and conditions rather than replacing them with stronger promotional language.

sections.title: Corrected audience-ready draft
paragraphs: The corrected body contains 135 words under the stated whitespace-token convention, excluding its heading. It falls within the required 100–150 word range.
The correction restores source facts, preserves the required quotation exactly, avoids invented logistics, and states the review status truthfully.

code.label: Corrected audience-ready draft, 135 body words
code.code:

The workshop has 30 places, and registration is required. The fee is $8 per participant. Residents age 60 or older may attend free. Residents who cannot pay may request a fee waiver when registering. A request is not guaranteed.

Registration opens April 20, 2026, through the North Harbor Community Workshop registration desk. Mina Ortiz said, "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying." The source provides no address, phone number, web address, or closing date. Review is pending.

sections.title: Trace the corrected output to its source
paragraphs: Traceability connects each important output sentence to exact evidence and a preservation decision. Sentence numbers refer only to the corrected draft body, not its heading.
This record lets another reviewer find the evidence without relying on the writer's confidence or memory.

code.label: Source-to-output traceability
code.code:
O1 | Source: "May 16, 2026" and "10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m." | Output sentence 1 | Exact date and schedule preserved.
O2 | Source: "North Harbor residents" and "basic repair skills for small household items" | Output sentence 2 | Audience and purpose preserved.
O3 | Source: "not a drop-off repair service" | Output sentence 3 | Limitation preserved exactly.
O4 | Source: "one small item" and no promised outcome | Output sentence 4 | Scope preserved; guarantee avoided.
O5 | Source: "30 places" and "registration is required" | Output sentence 5 | Capacity and process preserved.
O6 | Source: "$8 per participant" | Output sentence 6 | Cost preserved.
O7 | Source: "Residents age 60 or older may attend free" | Output sentence 7 | Age-based condition preserved.
O8 | Source: "Residents who cannot pay may request a fee waiver when registering." | Output sentence 8 | Exact conditional sentence preserved, including final period.
O9 | Source: waiver request is not a guarantee | Output sentence 9 | No approval implied.
O10 | Source: registration opens April 20, 2026, through the registration desk | Output sentence 10 | Opening date and channel preserved.
O11 | Source: "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying." | Output sentence 11 | Exact quotation and attribution preserved.
O12 | Source: no address, telephone number, web address, or closing date | Output sentence 12 | Unknown logistics remain unknown.
O13 | Brief: coordinator review required; no approval documented | Output sentence 13 | Status is truthfully PENDING.

sections.title: Recover from drift and invention
paragraphs: Recovery should be limited to affected content. Return to the exact source evidence, restore the preservation rules, remove unsupported additions, and compare the repaired section again.
Do not fabricate an approval. A reviewer role may be assigned while the status remains pending. Broader legal, policy, safety, or reputational questions should be escalated to the responsible owner.

code.label: Scoped recovery and change record
code.code:
Record ID: repair-lab-recovery-01
Source: Saturday Repair Lab, fictional practice passage, version 1.
Brief: Filled transformation brief, version 1.
Affected scope: Announcement body only.
Detected drift: 1:00 p.m. became 2:00 p.m.; 30 places became 40; residents became everyone; the $8 fee and age-60 condition disappeared; a waiver request became implied receipt; teaching became staff repair; unsupported logistics, a web address, and a closing date were added.
Root-cause hypothesis: The flawed draft followed familiar promotional patterns instead of treating absent details as unknown. This is an instructional hypothesis, not evidence from an actual model run.
Change applied: Restored exact schedule, capacity, eligibility, fee, conditions, registration facts, limitation, and quotation; deleted unsupported additions; revised only the announcement body.
Evidence: Corrected draft plus traceability entries O1–O13.
Review owner: Workshop coordinator.
Review status: PENDING. No reviewer approval or completion is asserted.
Remaining limitations: Address, phone number, web address, closing date, tools, parts, food, parking, childcare, accepted-item list, and repair outcome remain UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Protect authors, subjects, and readers
paragraphs: Minimize sensitive material, preserve attribution, respect copyright and confidentiality, and avoid deceptive impersonation. Check quotations and citations against their originals before publication. Record permission, source version, brief version, changes, limitations, reviewer role, and actual review status.

Official prompting documentation supports clear instructions, constraints, examples, structured separation, message roles, and specified output formats. These practices can improve organization, but they do not establish factual accuracy or replace source comparison. Behavior can differ across models and versions, including Meta Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, and Mistral, so transfer should be tested rather than assumed.
This module's source and drafts are fictional teaching artifacts. No model execution or reviewer completion is claimed.
sections.callout: Transformation is successful only when the intended meaning survives.

code.label: Publication safety checklist
code.code:
Permission confirmed: YES for this fictional lesson source.
Sensitive data minimized: YES; no real private data supplied.
Source version recorded: YES.
Brief version recorded: YES.
Exact quotations checked: YES against the visible fictional source.
Dates, numbers, costs, and conditions checked: YES in the audit.
Unsupported logistics removed: YES.
Accessibility review: PENDING responsible review.
Publication review: PENDING workshop coordinator review.
AI or tool disclosure: Apply the publisher's documented policy; no policy is supplied here.
Approval claimed: NO.

sections.title: Execute in visible passes
paragraphs: After extraction, transform the source under the brief. Keep facts, draft, and audit separate so a reviewer can distinguish source evidence from generated wording.

The copyable prompt below includes the exact supplied source and the filled brief. It is for offline practice and does not claim an actual model run. The reusable blank template is placed at the end of the same code block.

sections.title: Practice task: changed source facts
paragraphs: Complete this separate task before reading the answer key. The changed facts are authoritative for this variation and supersede conflicting baseline facts, especially the original fee, free-attendance rule, and waiver condition.

Write a 100–150 word announcement and a short audit identifying at least four changes from the baseline. Preserve the changed conditional payment sentence exactly. Do not invent a venue, contact details, closing date, amenities, item list, or repair guarantee.

code.label: Authoritative changed input and learner task
code.code:
CHANGED SOURCE FACTS

Organization: North Harbor Community Workshop.
Date and schedule: Sunday, June 7, 2026, from 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. The session is two hours.
Eligibility and capacity: North Harbor residents age 16 or older; 24 places; registration is required.
Cost: $12 per participant. This replaces the original $8 fee and the original free-attendance condition for residents age 60 or older.
Changed conditional payment rule: "Residents age 70 or older may request a fee waiver when registering; a waiver is not automatic." This sentence fully supersedes the original age-60 free-attendance rule and the original inability-to-pay waiver rule.
Registration: Opens May 1, 2026, through the registration desk.
Activity: Participants may practice on one small item they bring. It remains a teaching session, not a drop-off repair service, and repair is not guaranteed.
Required exact quotation: Mina Ortiz said, "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying."
Unknowns: Address, phone number, web address, closing date, tools, replacement parts, food, parking, childcare, accepted items, and whether a waiver request will be granted.

TASK
1. Write a 100–150 word audience-ready announcement using only these changed facts.
2. Copy the changed conditional payment sentence exactly.
3. Preserve the required quotation exactly.
4. Audit at least four facts that changed from the baseline.
5. Name one detail that you deliberately left unknown.

sections.title: Changed-input audit and feedback
paragraphs: Compare your work only after completing the practice task. The evidence below identifies observable changes and provides correction advice for common stale facts.

A strong response preserves conditional force and unknowns. If your draft says the workshop is free, uses the old schedule, or promises that a waiver will be granted, revise the affected sentence rather than rewriting unrelated content.

code.label: Full changed-input audit and specific feedback
code.code:
C1 | Baseline: Saturday, May 16, 2026 | Changed result: Sunday, June 7, 2026 | Pass if both day and date changed.
C2 | Baseline: 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., three hours | Changed result: 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m., two hours | Replace every stale endpoint or duration.
C3 | Baseline: North Harbor residents, with no minimum age under 60 stated | Changed result: North Harbor residents age 16 or older | Add 16-or-older eligibility; do not say everyone.
C4 | Baseline: 30 places | Changed result: 24 places | Replace 30 with 24.
C5 | Baseline: $8 per participant | Changed result: $12 per participant | Replace $8 with $12.
C6 | Baseline: residents age 60 or older attend free, while residents unable to pay may request a waiver | Changed result: "Residents age 70 or older may request a fee waiver when registering; a waiver is not automatic." | Delete both superseded baseline rules and preserve this changed sentence exactly.
C7 | Baseline: registration opens April 20, 2026 | Changed result: registration opens May 1, 2026 | Replace the opening date.
C8 | Preserved quotation: "Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying." | Pass only if wording and punctuation match exactly.
C9 | Deliberately unknown detail: address | Pass because neither source supplies an address.
Feedback: If your draft says free attendance, 30 places, age 60, inability-to-pay eligibility, April 20, Saturday, or May 16, it contains stale baseline information. If it says a waiver will be granted, it strengthens a request into a guarantee. If it adds a link, address, deadline, amenity, accepted-item list, or successful repair, delete the unsupported claim.

activity.title: Transform and audit a source passage
instructions: Read the complete fictional source passage and filled transformation brief.
Use the first-pass ledger to distinguish source evidence from wording choices.
Compare the intentionally flawed draft with the source and identify exact drift, changed conditions, and unsupported additions.
Check the corrected 100–150 word draft against the traceability record.
Complete the separate changed-input task before reading its answer key and feedback.
Work offline with paper or a text editor. No paid account, model, external file, or internet connection is required.
evidence: A completed transformation brief with audience, purpose, transformation type, source of truth, preservation rules, prohibited additions, and review owner.
A first-pass fact ledger quoting exact source evidence.
A source-to-draft audit explaining exact drift and unsupported additions.
A corrected 100–150 word draft with source-to-output traceability.
A scoped recovery record whose review status remains pending.
A genuinely changed practice draft and audit based on the authoritative changed input.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which sentence sounded smoother after transformation but changed a condition, promise, or unknown, and what exact source wording corrected it?

cues.text: Start with the brief. It names the audience, purpose, channel, transformation, source of truth, exact facts to preserve, prohibited additions, unknowns, review owner, and pending status. These fields define what may change and how the result will be checked.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The filled brief is shown as structured text with audience, purpose, source, preservation rules, prohibited additions, unknowns, and review status.

cues.text: Static text visual: Audience and purpose -> source of truth -> fact ledger -> constrained draft -> evidence audit -> scoped recovery -> responsible review.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A linear process reads audience and purpose, source of truth, fact ledger, constrained draft, evidence audit, scoped recovery, and responsible review.

cues.text: This is a fictional, permission-safe source, not a real announcement and not a recorded model run. Its deliberate unknowns matter. The source states May 16, 2026, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., 30 places, an $8 fee, an age-60 free-attendance condition, a conditional waiver request, and a required quotation. It does not supply an address, web address, closing date, amenities, accepted-item list, or repair guarantee.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The complete fictional source passage is available as text, including its facts, limitations, quotation, and deliberate unknowns.

cues.text: Static fact card: May 16, 2026; 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.; 30 places; $8; residents age 60 or older may attend free; waiver requests are not guaranteed.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The fact card lists the date, time, capacity, fee, age condition, and non-guaranteed waiver condition in a linear list.

cues.text: Before drafting, extract evidence. For example, the source says, “Residents who cannot pay may request a fee waiver when registering.” The ledger records that quote, identifies it as a conditional payment rule, and says to copy it exactly. It also records UNKNOWN for absent logistics. Extraction separates evidence from later wording choices.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The ledger pairs each source quotation with its meaning and preservation rule.

cues.text: Question: What should the ledger record when the source gives no web address? Answer: UNKNOWN, not a guessed address. Feedback: absence of evidence is a constraint on the draft.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The question, answer, and feedback are displayed together as text.

cues.text: Now examine the supplied flawed draft. It says 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., first 40 people, everyone, free for all residents, and staff repair. It also promises tools, parts, refreshments, parking, childcare, a website, and a May 1 deadline. These are observable changes or inventions, not evidence of an actual model execution.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The intentionally flawed draft is shown in full and labeled as supplied teaching material, not an actual model output.

cues.text: The audit explains consequences. Changing 1:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. adds an hour. Changing 30 places to 40 changes capacity. “Everyone” removes the North Harbor residency condition. “Free for all residents” removes both the $8 fee and the age-60 condition. “Our staff will repair it for you” changes a teaching session into a service and guarantee. Unsupported logistics must be deleted.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The audit displays paired source and draft evidence with the consequence of each difference.

cues.text: Question: Why is “may request” not equivalent to “will receive”? Answer: a request can be denied, so receipt is not guaranteed. Correction feedback: preserve modal words and conditions instead of strengthening them into promotional promises.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The checkpoint question, answer, and correction feedback are available as text.

cues.text: The corrected body contains 135 words, excluding its heading. Listen to the key repair: “The workshop has 30 places, and registration is required. The fee is $8 per participant. Residents age 60 or older may attend free. Residents who cannot pay may request a fee waiver when registering. A request is not guaranteed.” This restores capacity, fee, age condition, exact waiver wording, and its limitation. It also keeps the exact quotation, “Bring curiosity, not confidence; we will learn by trying.”

A reviewer can follow the evidence without relying on confidence or memory.

Its root-cause statement is explicitly an instructional hypothesis.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The recovery record shows affected scope, detected drift, changes, evidence, review owner, pending status, and remaining unknowns.

cues.text: Safety includes permission, minimization, attribution, quotation checking, disclosure, and truthful review status. This lesson uses fictional material. No model execution, paid tool use, internet lookup, or reviewer approval is claimed. Prompt behavior can vary across models and versions, so a prompt pattern is not proof of accuracy. The source, version, changes, limitations, and responsible review state should remain documented.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The safety checklist is displayed as text with permission, minimization, quotation checking, pending review, and no approval claimed.

cues.text: The section below contains a complete copyable prompt, the exact supplied source, the filled brief, and a reusable blank template at the end. The prompt asks for a fact ledger, draft, and audit. Official OpenAI documentation describes prompt engineering as writing instructions for consistent output and says instructions can have higher priority than input. Anthropic recommends clear constraints, examples, XML structure, and explicit roles. Google documents clear instructions, response formats, and few-shot examples. These techniques organize work, but none replaces comparison with the source.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The replacement section provides the prompt, exact source, filled brief, and blank template as copyable text.

cues.text: Static comparison visual: source quote “10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.” -> draft candidate -> audit result: preserve exact schedule.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The visual shows one source quote flowing to a draft candidate and then to an audit decision.

cues.text: Mark one exact quotation, one payment condition, and one unknown in the supplied source. You may write, type, or say your three choices.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: Learners can mark three items on paper, in a text editor, or aloud.

cues.text: Pause for 90 seconds.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A ninety-second learner pause is provided.

cues.text: The practice task is a genuinely changed input. Its authoritative result is Sunday, June 7, 2026, from 1:30 p.m. to 3:30 p.m., a two-hour session for North Harbor residents age 16 or older, with 24 places and a $12 fee. Registration opens May 1. The new payment rule is not the old age-60 rule or the old inability-to-pay rule.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The changed facts are shown in full, including date, time, duration, age, capacity, fee, waiver rule, and registration date.

cues.text: Write a 100–150 word announcement and audit before viewing the key. Preserve exactly: “Residents age 70 or older may request a fee waiver when registering; a waiver is not automatic.” Also preserve the quotation and leave one supplied unknown unnamed in your draft.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: Learners may complete the announcement and audit on paper or in a text editor.

cues.text: Pause for 120 seconds.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A one-hundred-twenty-second learner pause is provided.

cues.text: Now read the answer key after the pause. Its body contains 129 words, excluding the heading. The changed result uses Sunday, June 7, 1:30 to 3:30, two hours, age 16 or older, 24 places, $12, the exact age-70 waiver sentence, and May 1. It does not use the stale Saturday, May 16, age-60, $8, 30-place, or April 20 facts.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The complete changed-input answer is shown after the learner pause and is labeled as one acceptable response.

cues.text: Static changed-key comparison: Saturday -> Sunday; May 16 -> June 7; 10:00–1:00 -> 1:30–3:30; 30 -> 24; $8 -> $12; age 60 -> age 70 request; April 20 -> May 1.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The comparison lists each baseline value beside its changed value in order.

cues.text: Use the feedback as correction, not as a score guess. A draft fails if it says free attendance, 30 places, age 60, April 20, Saturday, or May 16. It also fails if it says a waiver will be granted. Delete invented links, addresses, deadlines, amenities, accepted-item lists, and repair outcomes. Change only the affected sentences, then audit again.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The changed-input audit lists each changed fact and gives specific feedback for stale facts, guarantees, and unsupported additions.

cues.text: Question: Which two payment statements must not appear in the changed answer? Answer: the baseline age-60 free-attendance rule and the baseline inability-to-pay waiver rule. Feedback: both are superseded by the exact age-70 conditional sentence.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The payment checkpoint and feedback are displayed as text.

cues.text: Begin the five-question check. Use the source, ledger, audit, changed answer, and feedback as evidence. Remember that a truthful pending status is different from approval.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: The assessment handoff is shown as text before the five-question knowledge check.

questions.prompt: What should a transformation brief identify first?
choices: The audience, purpose, transformation type, source of truth, preservation rules, and review
questions.explanation: These fields define what may change, what must remain exact, which additions are prohibited, and who owns review.

questions.prompt: Why use separate extraction and transformation passes?
choices: To distinguish source-derived facts from rewriting and proposed additions
questions.explanation: A visible extraction pass makes source facts, conditions, quotations, and unknowns easier to compare with the later draft. It does not guarantee approval.

questions.prompt: A plain-language rewrite changes a legal obligation. What should happen?
choices: Keep it because it is easier to read
Return to the source, correct the affected section, and obtain responsible review
questions.explanation: Readability cannot override exact consequential meaning. Correct the affected scope against the source and submit it for responsible review.

questions.prompt: Which practice best protects sensitive source material?
choices: Ask the model not to remember it
Minimize and redact data, confirm permission, and use approved handling
questions.explanation: Data minimization, permission, redaction, and approved handling reduce exposure before transformation begins.

questions.prompt: What makes a transformation correction reproducible?
choices: A record of source version, brief version, detected drift, fix, evidence, and reviewer status
questions.explanation: Versioned source material, instructions, detected drift, scoped changes, supporting evidence, and truthful review status allow the correction to be reconstructed.
